findings.span: Stock up on Vitamin B5 10% Moisturizer Offer as on beminimalist.co, 2 Oct 2026.
findings.why: This closing line is a template glitch: it repeats the headline a third time, runs it into a fragment ('Moisturizer Offer as on'), and restates the date already given in the first sentence. Broken copy like this would not pass a brand review.
findings.fix: Delete it; the first sentence already carries the offer, the site, the date and 'T&C apply'.

tone_read: A calm offer ad: no countdown, 'hurry' or scarcity wording, and the free item's condition and 'T&C apply' are stated. But 'Stock up' three times and 'offer as captured on 2 Oct 2026' (internal tooling language; 'as on 2 Oct 2026' reads naturally) make the copy feel machine-assembled rather than clean and declarative.
language_read: The product line is accurate to the page ('a lightweight, oil-free everyday moisturizer with 10% Vitamin B5 (Panthenol)'), with the concentration on-format and the active named precisely. There are no efficacy claims to hedge and no natural or chemical-free framing, and the offer wording matches the captured 'Buy 2, Get 3rd Free' exactly.
